title: Nothing Left Behind: Finding Evidence from a Large Randomized Evaluation Corpus
abstract: arXiv:2610.36910v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Many AI systems need to find every relevant items in a large collection and then organize what they found. The standard way to do this is to tag each item with labels from a curated vocabulary and search on those labels. Those labels are useful for organizing results, but searching on them misses items that do not fit a label and returns too much when labels are broad. We compare this approach with an embedding-based approach: find candidates by meaning using text embeddings, then have a language model keep only the relevant ones. In a corpus of 7,354 randomized trials, label search found 45% of the evidence a systematic review would include, while the new approach found 92%, at a cost per query that rises with search depth. These results support a two-stage architecture that combines broad candidate retrieval with query-specific evidence filtering.

translated_title: 不遗漏任何内容：从大型随机评估语料库中寻找证据
translated_abstract: 许多AI系统需要在大规模集合中找出所有相关条目，然后对找到的内容进行整理。标准做法是使用人工整理的词表为每个条目打上标签，再基于这些标签进行搜索。这些标签虽然有助于组织结果，但基于标签的搜索会遗漏不符合任何标签的条目，而当标签过于宽泛时又会返回过多结果。我们将该方法与一种基于嵌入的方法进行了比较：利用文本嵌入按语义寻找候选条目，再由语言模型仅保留相关条目。在一个包含7,354项随机试验的语料库中，标签搜索仅找到了系统性综述所纳入证据的45%，而新方法找到了92%，其每次查询的成本随搜索深度增加而上升。这些结果支持一种将宽泛的候选检索与针对特定查询的证据过滤相结合的两阶段架构。
tldr: 该论文提出一种结合文本嵌入候选检索与语言模型证据过滤的两阶段方法，在7,354项随机试验语料库中找到了系统性综述应纳入证据的92%，远超传统标签搜索的45%。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a two-stage approach combining embedding-based candidate retrieval with language-model evidence filtering, which finds 92% of the evidence a systematic review would include in a corpus of 7,354 randomized trials, far exceeding the 45% found by traditional label-based search.
